title: Boeuf Bourguignon
subtitle: Burgundian braised beef with red wine
excerpt: Beef braised low and slow in red wine with bacon, mushrooms, and pearl onions until the sauce is deep and glossy. A French classic that takes most of a day but needs little attention.

recipe.sourceNotes: Boeuf bourguignon is the signature slow-braised beef dish of Burgundy, where the wine and the cattle are both prized. It was brought to wide English-language attention by Julia Child's Mastering the Art of French Cooking (1961).

recipeTools.notes: A large heavy pot that can go from hob to oven.

content.text: Boeuf bourguignon is beef braised in red wine with smoked bacon, mushrooms, and pearl onions. The wine reduces into a deeply savoury sauce that coats the tender chunks of beef. Like most braises, it is best made a day ahead, then reheated so the sauce can settle and the beef can absorb more flavour.

Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Toss the beef with the flour, salt, and pepper. Heat the oil in a large dutch oven over a high heat. Brown the beef in three batches, about 3 minutes per batch. Lift out and set aside.

Add the bacon lardons to the pot and fry for 3 minutes until starting to crisp. Add the chopped onion and carrot. Cook for 6 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and tomato puree and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and stock. Scrape up the browned bits. Return the beef, add the thyme and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook in the oven for 2 hours.

While the beef braises, melt the butter in a frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the pearl onions for 8 minutes until golden, shaking the pan occasionally. In the same pan, fry the mushrooms for 4 minutes until golden. Set both aside.

After 2 hours, the beef should be nearly tender. Add the pearl onions and mushrooms to the pot. Return to the oven uncovered for a further 30 minutes until the sauce has reduced and the beef is completely tender.
Remove the thyme stalks and bay leaves. Taste for seasoning, scatter over the parsley, and serve.
